bullets.title: Nasdaq 100 futures slip 0.5% as session opens weak
bullets.body: Nasdaq 100 futures extended declines to 0.5% in the morning session, while SPY notched its first up day in four with re-accelerating volume — setting up a mixed tape for tech-heavy names.

bullets.title: AI capex boom called largest GDP driver in history (Bloomberg)
bullets.body: Bloomberg and multiple fintwit accounts flagged that AI infrastructure investment — spanning data centers, chips, cloud, and energy — is generating the biggest capex-driven GDP boost on record. Separately, Mag7/Neural9 names are showing meaningful divergence in price action, ending the era of monolithic mega-cap tech moves.

bullets.title: META quietly among MSFT's largest AI customers
bullets.body: Reports circulating on fintwit that Meta has become one of Microsoft's largest AI customers, with the partnership having proceeded without major public announcements.

bullets.title: Alibaba Q1 beats revenue/EBITDA but EPS misses sharply; AI chip adoption broadening
bullets.body: Alibaba Q1 revenue of 268.95B yuan beat the 268.52B yuan estimate and adj EBITDA of 39.14B yuan topped the 36.92B estimate, but adj EPS of 8.52 yuan badly missed the 11.28 yuan consensus. The company highlighted broad commercial adoption of its Zhenwu AI chips and sustained full-stack AI investment. ADRs erased early losses to trade +0.5%.

bullets.title: Walmart Q2 comp sales miss weighs on consumer sentiment read
bullets.body: Walmart US comp sales ex-gas came in at +2.6% vs. the +3.67% consensus, though adj EPS of $0.81 beat the $0.74 estimate and revenue of $187.94B edged above the $186.87B forecast. Q3 EPS guidance of $0.62–$0.64 missed the $0.68 estimate; FY adj EPS raised to $2.80–$2.87 from $2.75–$2.85. The comp miss is a notable read-through for consumer spending.

bullets.title: 30Y UST yields rebound to 5.23% after prior-day drop; Treasury buybacks may only briefly tame curve
bullets.body: Thirty-year Treasury yields rose 4bps to 5.23% after a 9bps drop the prior session. Commentary suggests Treasury wants the long end controlled and is using the dollar as an economic release valve. Analysis warns buyback programs may provide only temporary yield relief.

bullets.title: US national debt crosses $40 trillion; $3.8B/day in interest payments
bullets.body: US national debt hit a record $40 trillion amid historically fast borrowing. The government now spends $3.8B per day on interest — exceeding $3.1B/day on Medicare and $2.5B/day on Defense — stoking growing investor concern over fiscal sustainability.

bullets.title: German 5Y yield hits 3% for first time since 2008; European gas spikes to €65/MWh
bullets.body: German 5-year yields reached 3% for the first time since 2008, signaling tighter European monetary conditions. Simultaneously, European natural gas prices hit €65/MWh — the highest since March — though the EU Commission noted storage is at 62% with no immediate supply concern.

bullets.title: Healthcare most-shorted basket surges 6.4% in a day, +31.5% over 3 months
bullets.body: The 'Healthcare Most Short' consensus hedge-fund basket ripped 6.4% in a single session and is up 31.5% over the past three months on short-squeeze momentum. The healthcare sector overall was called one of the best relative days in market history vs. tech.

bullets.title: High-beta momentum stocks down 7.3%; hedge fund pessimism tracks short books
bullets.body: A high-beta momentum index fell 7.3% in the prior session. Fintwit commentary notes that hedge fund bearishness tends to reflect the composition of their own short books rather than independent macro views.

bullets.title: Crypto short liquidations hit record $2.73B; BTC crosses 200-day MA at $71K
bullets.body: Yesterday's crypto surge triggered $2.73B in short liquidations across perpetuals — flagged as the largest such event on record. Bitcoin subsequently climbed above its 200-day moving average and reached $71,000. Crypto stocks were also surging premarket following a White House meeting.

bullets.title: CCL/advanced laminate supply capacity expanding but running behind schedule
bullets.body: Taiwan-based DigiTimes reports that suppliers in Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and China are expanding advanced copper-clad laminate (CCL) production capacity, but additions are running behind schedule amid existing supply shortages and higher margins.

bullets.title: CrowdStrike CTO departing to launch AI-cyber fund
bullets.body: CrowdStrike's CTO is leaving the company to launch a new AI-focused cybersecurity fund — a potential signal of accelerating private capital formation in the AI-security space.

bullets.title: Amazon market cap now exceeds Walmart's
bullets.body: Fintwit noted that Amazon's market capitalization has surpassed Walmart's, a milestone commentary tied to Amazon's scale gains across e-commerce and cloud.

bullets.title: Retail leverage rotating out of AI stocks into biotech; SK Hynix buybacks supporting EWY
bullets.body: One fintwit trader flagged that leveraged retail money is rotating from AI stocks into biotech names like MRNA. SK Hynix buybacks were cited as a support factor for EWY, with Samsung Foundry trading in a 10–15% range.

bullets.title: Unitree IPO surges from $9.1B to ~$50B on debut; humanoid mass market within a decade
bullets.body: Chinese humanoid robotics firm Unitree went public at a $9.1B valuation and surged to approximately $50B on its first trading day. The founder projects humanoid robots will reach mass-market status within a decade, even as IPO momentum in the sector shows early signs of fading.

bullets.title: SPY volume re-accelerates on first up day in four
bullets.body: SPY posted its first up day after four consecutive declining sessions, with volume notably re-accelerating — a constructive technical signal watched by fintwit momentum traders.

bullets.title: Tanker seized in Gulf of Aden; Iran losing Strait of Hormuz control per CNN
bullets.body: Armed persons took control of a tanker in the Gulf of Aden per UKMTO alerts. Separately, CNN reports Iran has lost significant control of the Strait of Hormuz — a potential tail risk for oil supply routes and energy prices.
